rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the king spoke seventy languages and Yusuf answered each in that language; Yusuf was thirty, impressing the king with his knowledge of the dream.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: وكان الملك يتكلم بسبعين لسانا، فكلما كلم يوسف بلسان أجابه يوسف بذلك اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king asked Yusuf to recount the dream orally, and Yusuf described the seven fat cows, seven gaunt cows, and seven green and black ears of grain.
rows.anchor: إني أحب أن أسمع رؤياي منك شفاها، فقال له يوسف: نعم، أيها الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf recommends sowing abundantly in the fertile years and storing the harvest in its stalks, which can also feed animals.
rows.anchor: أرى أن تجمع الطعام، وتزرع الزرع الكثير في هذه السنين المخصبة وتبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He advises collecting one fifth of people's food, enough for Egypt and neighboring lands, while visitors buy provisions and enlarge the treasury.
rows.anchor: وتأمر الناس فيرفعون من طعامهم الخمس فيكفيك من الطعام الذي جمعته لأهل مصر ومن حولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the king asks who can manage the work, Yusuf offers himself to oversee the land's storehouses; the gloss takes the phrase as the king's storehouses.
rows.anchor: فقال: يوسف اجعلني على خزائن الأرض مجاز الآية: على خزائن أرضك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poems present Yusuf as a model: patient endurance in prison eventually led him to kingship.
rows.anchor: أما في رسول الله يوسف أسوة … لمثلك محبوسا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A letter to a friend says relief follows fear and grief, and urges him not to despair because God gave Yusuf the storehouses after prison.
rows.anchor: وراء مضيق الخوف متسع الأمن … وأول مفروح به آخر الحزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons mean that Jacob keeps remembering Yusuf and never stops loving him.
rows.anchor: قالوا يعني ولد يعقوب تالله تفتؤا تذكر يوسف أي لا تزال تذكر يوسف

rows.speaker: أوس بن حجر
rows.claim: Aus uses فتئت to mean continuing or not ceasing, as in the image of dust rising like a canopy.
rows.anchor: قال أوس بن حجر: فما فتئت حي كأن غبارها … سرادق يوم ذي رياج ترفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poem likewise uses فما فتئت for continuing to return and pursue.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: فما فتئت خيل تثوب وتدعي … ويلحق منها لا حق وتقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative لا is omitted with فتئ, so the phrase means I will not cease sitting, as the cited Imru al-Qays line shows.
rows.anchor: وحذف (لا) قوله فتئ كقول امرئ القيس

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays uses أبرح with an understood لا, meaning he will not stop sitting even if beheaded.
rows.anchor: فقلت يمين الله أبرح قاعدا … ولو قطعوا رأسي لديك وأوصالي

rows.speaker: خداش بن زهير
rows.claim: Khudash's line also illustrates أبرح with an understood لا, meaning I will remain as long as my people endure.
rows.anchor: وقال خداش بن زهير: وأبرح ما أدام الله قومي … بحمد الله منتطقا مجيدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses حرض as seriously ill and weakened.
rows.anchor: حتى تكون حرضا اختلف ألفاظ المفسرين فيه، فقال ابن عباس: دنفا

rows.speaker: العوفي
rows.claim: Al-Awfi explains حرض as weakened by illness.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: دنفا، العوفي: يعني الهد في المرض

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says حرض is the state just short of death.
rows.anchor: العوفي: يعني الهد في المرض، مجاهد: هو ما دون الموت، يعني قريبا من الموت

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses حرض as old age.
rows.anchor: قتادة: هرما، الضحاك: باليا مدبرا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says it means worn out and deteriorated.
rows.anchor: قتادة: هرما، الضحاك: باليا مدبرا

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the person is ruined and no longer able to work.
rows.anchor: ابن إسحاق: فاسدا لا عمل لك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd defines حرض as someone reduced to the most decrepit age and unable to reason.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: الحرض: الذي قد رد إلى أرذل العمر حتى لا يعقل

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas describes the skin dried over the bones.
rows.anchor: الربيع بن أنس: يابس الجلد على العظم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses حرض as seriously ill.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: مدنفا، الكسائي

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i defines حرض as corrupted and without good in it.
rows.anchor: الكسائي: الحرض: الفاسد الذي لا خير فيه

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the person is gone or wasted away.
rows.anchor: الأخفش: يعني ذاهبا

rows.speaker: المخرج
rows.claim: Al-Mukhraj explains the word as melted by grief.
rows.anchor: المخرج: ذائبا من الهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra transmits a gloss from an unnamed authority: weak and unable to move.
rows.anchor: الفراء عن بعضهم: ضعيفا لا حراك بك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan compares the person to a battered, broken waterskin.
rows.anchor: الحسن: كالشن المدقوق المكسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss calls the state exhausting and debilitating.
rows.anchor: علام تعبا مضنى، ابن الأنباري: هالكا فاسدا

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the person is perishing and corrupted.
rows.anchor: ابن الأنباري: هالكا فاسدا

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi glosses حرض as fallen or collapsed.
rows.anchor: القتيبي: ساقطا، وكلها متقاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The combined sense is a body weakened by illness and a mind deranged; the underlying corruption may come from grief, love, or old age.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: حتى يكون دنف الجسم مخبول العقل، وأصل الحرض: الفساد في الجسم أو العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حرض is a verbal noun used as a noun, so its form stays the same for singular, dual, plural, masculine, and feminine; some Arabs instead use gendered حارض and حارضة.
rows.anchor: لأنه مصدر وضع موضع الاسم، ومن العرب من يقول للذكر حارض وللأنثى حارضة

rows.speaker: العرجي
rows.claim: Al-Arji's verse uses أحرضني for being worn down by love until illness consumed him.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول العرجي: إني امرؤ لج بي حب فأحرضني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final verse uses محرضا for one ruined by prolonged pursuit, further illustrating the root.
rows.anchor: طلبته الخيل يوما كاملا … ولو آلفته لأضحى محرضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported story says a wolf told Jacob that the flesh of prophets and their children is forbidden to wolves.
rows.anchor: أرسل الله إليه ذئبا فسلم عليه وكلمه، فقال له يعقوب: أكلت ابني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob tells his sons to search for Yusuf and his brother; فتحسسوا means pursue or seek news, and Ibn Abbas glosses it as search for them.
rows.anchor: من يوسف وأخيه: وهو تفعلوا من الحس يعني تتبعوا، قال ابن عباس: التمسوا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and Qatada gloss روح الله as God's relief.
rows.anchor: من روح الله: من فرج الله، قال ابن زيد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses روح الله as God's mercy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد وقتادة، والضحاك: من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes the terms by saying tahassus is seeking good, while tajassus seeks bad.
rows.anchor: سئل ابن عباس عن الفرق بين التجسس والتحسس فقال: لا يبعد أحدهما عن الآخر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada report that Jacob always maintained good expectations of God after every trial and never thought ill of Him.
rows.anchor: الحسن وقتادة: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله يعقوب لم ينزل به بلاء قط إلا أتى حسن ظنه بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report continuing from the prior excerpt, Jacob's son says he consoled himself with a younger maternal brother; after that brother was taken, Yusuf wept at the brothers' accusation and threat.
rows.anchor: ثم كان لي ابن وكان أخاه من أمه وكنت أتسلى به، فذهبوا به ثم رجعوا وقالوا: إنه سرق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another account says Benjamin named three sons Yusuf, Wolf, and Blood so he would remember Joseph; Yusuf choked up, then asked what they had done to Joseph and his brother.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إنما قال ذلك حين سأل أخاه بنيامين: هل لك ولد؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says a sinner is ignorant at the moment of sin, even when acting deliberately.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يكون المذنب جاهل وقت ذنبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets إذ أنتم جاهلون as meaning they were children.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إذا أنتم صبيان، الحسن: شبان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the brothers as young men; the author finds this plausible because youth is especially associated with ignorance.
rows.anchor: الحسن: شبان وهذا غير بعيد من الصواب لأن مظنة الجهل الشباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers could be blamed for Benjamin's treatment because they accused him over the cup and said Rachel's sons were unlike them.
rows.anchor: فالجواب أنهم لما أطلقوا ألسنتهم على أخيهم بسبب الصاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that the brothers mistreated Benjamin after Joseph's loss because the two were from the same mother.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهما لما كانا من أم واحدة وكانوا يؤذونه بعد فقد يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن محصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muhaysin and Ibn Kathir read the opening as a statement, إنك, while the other readers use the interrogative.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن محصن وابن كثير: إنك على الخبر، وقرأ الآخرون على الاستفهام

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b's reading أو أنت يوسف supports the interrogative reading.
rows.anchor: ودليلهم قراءة أبي بن كعب أو أنت يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Yusuf's question uncovered the truth and lifted the veil, allowing the brothers to recognize him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: لما قال يوسف لأخوته هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف وأخيه الآية، كشف عنهم الغطاء

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: A report through al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas says Yusuf's pearl-like teeth when he smiled made the brothers associate him with Yusuf.
rows.anchor: جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس، قال: قال يوسف: هل علمتم ما فعلتم بيوسف

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A report through Ata from Ibn Abbas says the brothers recognized Yusuf after he removed his crown, revealing a white mark shared by Jacob, Isaac, and Sarah.
rows.anchor: ابن سمعان عن عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: إن إخوة يوسف لم يعرفوه حتى وضع التاج عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf says God favored the brothers and him by bringing them together after their separation.
rows.anchor: قال أنا يوسف وهذا أخي قد من الله علينا بأن جمع بيننا بعد ما فرقتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains piety as fulfilling obligations and avoiding sins, and patience as abstaining from what God forbids.
rows.anchor: إنه من يتق الله بأداء فرائضه واجتناب معاصيه، ويصبر عما حرم الله عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas specifies piety as avoiding adultery and patience as remaining celibate.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يتق الزنا ويصبر على العزوبة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says piety means avoiding God's disobedience and patience means enduring prison.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: يتق معصية الله ويصبر على السجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers admit Yusuf was favored over them in knowledge, judgment, intellect, virtue, beauty, and kingship.
rows.anchor: اختارك الله علينا بالعلم والحكم والعقل والفضل والحسن والملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خاطئين means guilty or sinful; the source gives its verb forms and cites Umayya's verse as evidence.
rows.anchor: لمخطئين، مذنبين، يقال: خطئ، يخطأ، خطأ وخطأ وأخطأ إذا أذنب

rows.speaker: أمية بن الأكسر
rows.claim: Umayya's line uses خطئا to mean they sinned.
rows.anchor: قال أمية بن الأكسر: وإن مهاجرين تكنفاه … لعمر الله قد خطئا وخابا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they missed the truth even though they acted intentionally; every sinner leaves the path of truth for doubt and disobedience.
rows.anchor: فقال: أخطئوا الحق وإن تعمدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf, being forbearing and guided, says there will be no blame or reproach and he will not recall their sin; تثريب originally means corruption and is Hijazi usage.
rows.anchor: لا تثريب عليكم اليوم لا تعيير ولا تأنيب عليكم، ولا أذكر لكم ذنبكم بعد اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's instruction about a slave woman who commits adultery uses لا يثرب to mean do not reproach her.
rows.anchor: إذا زنت أمة أحدكم فليجلدها الحد ولا يثرب عليها

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata transmits Ibn Abbas's report that at the conquest of Mecca the Prophet asked what the people expected and answered as Yusuf had: no blame today.
rows.anchor: عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: أخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعضادتي الباب يوم فتح مكة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and others say Yusuf learned that his father's eyes were gone and sent his shirt to be placed on Jacob's face, restoring his sight as a prayer.
rows.anchor: قال السدي وغيره: فلما عرفهم يوسف نفسه سألهم عن أبيه، فقال: ما فعل؟ قالوا: ذهبت عيناه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the shirt was woven in Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: كان ذلك القميص من نسج الجنة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A report from Mujahid says it was Abraham's garment from Paradise, passed through Isaac and Jacob; Gabriel told Yusuf to send it because its scent heals the sick.
rows.anchor: روى السدي عن أبيه عن مجاهد عن هذه الآية قال: كان يوسف أعلم بالله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujahid's account stresses that Yusuf knew God well enough not to think the shirt itself restored vision; its healing power came from its heavenly origin.
rows.anchor: كان يوسف أعلم بالله عز وجل من أن يعلم أن قميصه يرد على يعقوب بصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan set out from Arish in Egypt toward Canaan.
rows.anchor: ولما فصلت العير يعني خرجت من عريش مصر متوجهة إلى كنعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the wind asked God to carry Yusuf's scent to Jacob before the messenger arrived; God allowed it, and the wind carried the shirt's scent.
rows.anchor: روي أن الريح استأذنت ربها في أن تأتي يعقوب (عليه السلام) بريح يوسف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A report through al-Suddi from his father from Mujahid says Jacob sensed Yusuf's scent from a distance of three days.
rows.anchor: ابن السدي عن أبيه عن مجاهد، قال: أصاب يعقوب ريح يوسف من مسيرة ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jacob detected Yusuf's scent from eight nights away.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: وجد يعقوب ريح يوسف وهو منه على مسيرة ثماني ليال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas places the scent's distance between Basra and Kufa.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية قال: وجد ريحه من مسيرة ما بين البصرة والكوفة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the distance between Jacob and Yusuf was eighty farsakhs.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: ذكر لنا أنه كان بينهما يومئذ ثمانون فرسخا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses لولا أن تفندون as fearing that others will deem Jacob's judgment foolish.
rows.anchor: سفيان عن حصيف، عن مجاهد لولا أن تفندون، قال: تسفهون الرأي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as fearing they will consider him ignorant.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: تجهلون

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Najih report Mujahid's gloss: unless they say Jacob has lost his mind.
rows.anchor: ابن جريج وابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد: لولا أن تقولوا ذهب عقلك

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak say it means unless they call Jacob a liar; al-Awfi also transmits that gloss from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: سعيد بن جبير والسدي ولضحاك: تكذبون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret تفندون as growing old; another report from Mujahid gives the same sense.
rows.anchor: والحسن وقتادة: تهرمون، ومثله روى إسرائيل عن أبي يحيى عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: ربيع
rows.claim: Rabi glosses it as being called foolish or mad.
rows.anchor: ربيع: تحمقون

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Juwaybir's report from al-Dahhak explains the phrase as fearing they will say Jacob is senile and has lost his reason.
rows.anchor: جويبر عن الضحاك: تهرمون، فتقولون: شيخ كبير قد خرف وذهب عقله

rows.speaker: ابن يسار
rows.claim: Ibn Yasar says it means they will weaken or find Jacob feeble.
rows.anchor: ابن يسار: تضعفون

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala glosses it as finding Jacob disgraceful.
rows.anchor: أبو عمرو بن العلاء: تقبحون

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i interprets the word as incapacity or inability.
rows.anchor: الكسائي: تعجزون

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says it means blaming Jacob.
rows.anchor: الأخفش: تلومون

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses it as leading Jacob astray or deeming him deluded.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: تضللون، وأصل الفند: الفساد

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha uses الفند for corruption, supporting the word's root sense.
rows.anchor: قال النابغة: إلا سليمان إذ قال المليك له … قم في البرية فاحددها عن الفند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of الفند is corruption; blame is called tafnid, and the source cites several poems for that usage.
rows.anchor: أي أمنعها من الفساد، ولذلك يقال: اللوم تفنيد

rows.speaker: جرير بن عطية
rows.claim: Jarir's verse uses التفنيد for reproach or blame.
rows.anchor: وقال جرير بن عطية: يا عاذلي دعا الملام وأقصرا

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil uses الإفناد for the corruption caused by time.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول ابن مقبل: دع الدهر يفعل ما أراد فإنه … إذا كلف الافناد بالناس أفندا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons of Jacob are meant by قالوا, and they accuse their father of his old error: continued love for Yusuf.
rows.anchor: قالوا يعني أولاد أولاده تالله إنك لفي ضلالك خطأك القديم من حبك يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the bearer of glad tidings as Judah, Jacob's son.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: البريد يهوذا بن يعقوب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says the messenger arrived from the front of the caravan.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود: جاء البشير من بين يدي العير

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Judah volunteered to carry the shirt because he had previously taken the bloody shirt to Jacob and now wanted to bring him joy.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: قال يهوذا: أنا ذهبت بالقميص ملطخا بالدم إلى يعقوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Judah carried the shirt alone, ran barefoot and bareheaded, and covered eighty farsakhs with seven loaves still uneaten.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حمله يهوذا دونهم، وخرج حاسرا حافيا وجعل يعدو حتى أتى أباه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that the bearer was Malik ibn Dhuar from Midian.
rows.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس، قال: البشير مالك بن ذعر من أهل مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ألقاه means the messenger laid Yusuf's shirt on Jacob's face, and ارتد بصيرا means he regained sight after blindness.
rows.anchor: ألقاه يعني ألقى البشير قميص يوسف على وجه يعقوب، فارتد بصيرا: فعاد بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited graveyard greeting makes the exception apply to joining the dead, not to dying; alternatively, إن can mean إذ, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: عند دخول المقابر: «وإنا إن شاء الله بكم لاحقون»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source gives examples where إن is understood as إذ, including commands about usury, believers' superiority, and enslaved women seeking chastity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: (إن) هاهنا بمعنى (إذ) كقوله تعالى: وذروا ما بقي من الربا إن كنتم مؤمنين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the family entered safely because they had previously feared Egypt's rulers and lacked permission to enter.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: إنما قال: آمنين لأنهم فيما خلا كانوا يخافون ملوك مصر

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Yusuf welcomed his father and mother.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى آوى فقال ابن إسحاق: أباه وأمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say the two were Jacob and his aunt Leah; Rachel had died in childbirth, and Jacob married Rachel's sister, whom he called mother, as an uncle is called father.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: أبوه وخالته لعيا، وكانت راحيل أم يوسف قد ماتت في نفاسها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A report from al-Hasan says God raised Rachel from her grave so she could prostrate and fulfill Yusuf's dream.
rows.anchor: وروى إسحاق عن بشر عن سعيد عن الحسن، قال: نشر الله راحيل أم يوسف من قبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne is a seat on which Yusuf seated his parents; Ibn Ishaq alternatively says he elevated their status.
rows.anchor: ورفع أبويه على العرش على السرير، يعني أجلسهما عليه قال ابن إسحاق يعني رفع اسمهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob, Leah, and Yusuf's brothers bowed as a greeting customary then; this was a respectful bend, not worship or placing foreheads on the ground, which belongs to God alone.
rows.anchor: كانت تحية الناس يومئذ السجود، ولم يرد بالسجود وضع الجباه على الأرض

rows.speaker: الأعشى بن ثعلبة
rows.claim: Al-Asha's poem uses سجود for a gesture of greeting and respect.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الأعشى بن ثعلبة: فلما أتانا بعيد الكرى … سجدنا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another poem compares bowing to the prostration of Christians before their lords.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: فضول أزمتها لأمها أسجدت … سجود النصارى لأربابها

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha uses سجدا to mean hills made low and subdued under hooves, supporting the lexical sense of humility.
rows.anchor: وقيل: السجود في اللغة الخضوع كقول النابغة

rows.speaker: ثعلبة
rows.claim: Thalaba says خروا means they passed by, not fell to the ground; Mujahid agrees, while a report from Ibn Abbas says they prostrated to God.
rows.anchor: قال [ثعلبة] : خروا يعني مروا، ولم يرد الوقوع والسقوط على الأرض

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses خروا as passing by, while a report from Ibn Abbas takes the pronoun as God and the prostration as worship directed to Him.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: بمعنى المرور، وروي عن ابن عباس أن معناه خروا لله سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf recognizes the event as fulfillment of his earlier dream of eleven stars.
rows.anchor: هذا تأويل رءياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا، وهو قوله إني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators say that after his family reunited and his dream was fulfilled, Yusuf knew worldly power would end and therefore longed for the lasting joy of Paradise and prayed for death.
rows.anchor: علم أن ذلك لا يدوم له وأن لا بد له من فراقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer names Egypt's kingship, knowledge of dream interpretation, God as creator of heaven and earth and protector in both lives, and asks to die Muslim and join the prophetic forefathers.
rows.anchor: رب قد آتيتني من الملك يعني ملك مصر وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث يعني تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Yusuf died pure in Egypt and was placed in a marble coffin in the Nile; people disputed his burial, so they chose the river's source to share its blessing across Egypt.
rows.anchor: قيل: فتوفاه الله طيبا طاهرا بمصر، ودفن في النيل في صندوق رخام

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that the brothers feared their father's pardon might not secure God's pardon, so they asked Jacob and Yusuf to pray; the brothers stood humbled, and no answer came for twenty years.
rows.anchor: وروى صالح المري، عن يزيد الرقاشي عن أنس بن مالك، قال: إن الله عز وجل لما جمع ليعقوب شمله

rows.speaker: صالح المري
rows.claim: After twenty years, Gabriel told Jacob that God had answered his prayer, forgiven the brothers, and taken their pledge that they would become prophets after Jacob.
rows.anchor: قال صالح المري: يخيفهم، حتى إذا كان رأس العشرين نزل جبرئيل على يعقوب

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses خاف مقامي as fearing God's punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ذلك لمن خاف مقامي أي عذابي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say the communities asked God to punish the messengers if they were truthful, paralleling other demands for punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: يعني الأمم، وذلك أنهم قالوا: اللهم إن كان هؤلاء الرسل صادقين فعذبنا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say the messengers sought God's help against their people once they saw they would not believe, praying for their punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: يعني الرسل وذلك أنهم لما تبينوا من إيمان قومهم استنصروا عدوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is illustrated by God's stories of Noah, Lot, and Moses and by the destruction of every stubborn tyrant.
rows.anchor: بيانه قوله تعالى في قصة نوح ولوط وموسى وخاب كل جبار عنيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses عنيد as one who opposes and turns away from truth.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: معاند للحق ويجانبه

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim defines عنيد as one who veers away from the truth.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم: الناكب عن الحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says عنيد means turning away.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: المعرض

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada defines the stubborn rejecter as one who will not say there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: وقتادة: العنيد الذي لا يقول لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses عنيد as arrogant.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: المستكبر

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan describes the person as proudly defiant toward truth.
rows.anchor: ابن كيسان: الشامخ بالحق

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says عنيد means opposing the truth.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: المخالف للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, the stubborn camel leaves the path; أهل المعاني say عنيد is one who confronts another in opposition, from عند meaning a side.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: المعاند والعنيد هو المعارض لك بالخلاف وأصله من العند وهو الناحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arabic poem uses العند for the side or obstruction one cannot bear.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: إذا نزلت فاجعلوني وسطا … إني كبير لا أطيق العندا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من ورائه can mean in front of him, as in death lying ahead; the same usage appears in the verse about a king behind the travelers.
rows.anchor: من ورائه جهنم يعني أمامه وقدامه كما يقال: إن الموت من ورائك

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda calls وراء a word with opposite meanings.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: من الأضداد

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says وراء can mean something yet to come, as when someone says the other will come behind you.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: هو كما يقال هذا الآخر من ورائك أي سوف يأتيك

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil instead says Hell lies after the person.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: من ورائه جهنم يعني بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صديد is pus and blood; Qatada says it is what comes out between the disbeliever's skin and flesh.
rows.anchor: ويسقى من ماء ثم بين ذلك لنا فقال صديد وهو القيح والدم

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab and al-Rabi ibn Anas identify صديد as the drainage of Hell's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: محمد بن كعب والربيع بن أنس: هو غسالة أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned swallows the drink in repeated gulps rather than one, because of its bitterness and heat; لا يكاد يسيغه means he can scarcely swallow it.
rows.anchor: يتجرعه يتحساه ويشربه ويجرع لا بمرة واحدة لمرارته وحرارته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they do not like the drink; another view says the same.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يحبوه، وقيل لا يحبونه

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: Abu Umama transmits a Prophetic report: when the drink nears the condemned, it burns his face and scalp, then severs his intestines as he swallows it.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو أمامة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الآية يعطى إليه فيكرهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text links the hot drink severing intestines and the burning of faces to other Qur'anic descriptions.
rows.anchor: يقول الله وسقوا ماء حميما فقطع أمعاءهم وقال يشوي الوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death's pain and illness come to the condemned from every limb or place.
rows.anchor: ويأتيه الموت من كل مكان من أعضائه فيجد ألم الموت وسقمه

rows.speaker: إبراهيم التيمي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Taymi says the pain reaches from beneath every hair on the body.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم التيمي: حتى من تحت كل شعرة في جسده

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak locates the pain even in the big toe.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: حتى من إبهام رجله

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says death here names the torments that afflict the unbeliever in Hell.
rows.anchor: الأخفش: يعني البلايا التي تصيب الكافر في النار سماها موتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is not dead, so he cannot release his soul and rest.
rows.anchor: وما هو بميت ولا يخرج نفسه فيستريح

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the soul remains at the throat, unable to leave and cause death or return to the body and restore life.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: تعلق نفسه عند حنجرته فلا تخرج من فيه فيموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final phrase means another severe punishment awaits after this torment.
rows.anchor: ومن ورائه عذاب غليظ شديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse likens unbelievers' deeds to ash scattered by storm winds: what they earned gives them nothing, and this is far-reaching loss.
rows.anchor: مثل الذين كفروا بربهم أعمالهم كرماد اشتدت به الريح في يوم عاصف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains the syntax by attaching the likeness to the unbelievers while making their deeds the predicate, following Arabic word order that places the familiar subject first.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: أضاف المثل إلى الكافرين والمثل للأعمال لأن العرب تقدم الأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source compares the construction with verses where the order means God made every thing's creation beautiful and where the faces of those who lied against God are darkened.
rows.anchor: قوله: الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه أي أحسن خلق كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حاص means flee or turn away; محيص is an escape or way out.
rows.anchor: يقال حاص فلان عن كذا أي فر وزاغ عنه يحيص حيصا وحيوصا وحيصانا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the people of Hell alternate five hundred years of despair and five hundred years of patience, but neither helps; then they admit there is no escape.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: إنهم يقولون في النار تعالوا نجزع فيجزعون خمسمائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis speaks after the matter is finished, meaning after the people of Paradise and Hell have entered their destinations.
rows.anchor: قال الشيطان يعني إبليس لما قضي الأمر فرغ من الأمر فأدخل أهل الجنة الجنة وأهل النار النار

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says Iblis stands on a pulpit of fire as the unbelievers gather around him with their leaders.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يوضع له منبر من نار فيرقاه ويجتمع الكفار عليه بالأئمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis had no authority, kingdom, proof, or insight over them; the exception in إلا أن دعوتكم is disconnected and means he merely called them.
rows.anchor: وما كان لي عليكم من سلطان ولاية ومملكة وحجة وبصيرة إلا أن دعوتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بمصرخي means one who helps or rescues; most readers open the yā, while al-A'mash and Hamza kasra it.
rows.anchor: ما أنا بمصرخكم بمعينكم وما أنتم بمصرخي بمغني وبمغيثي

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash and Hamza read بمصرخي with a kasra; the form derives from بمصرخيين after dropping n and merging the yā endings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وحمزة: بكسر الياء، والأصل فيه بمصرخيين فذهبت النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatha follows the doubled consonant; the kasra resolves two vowelless letters because yā matches kasra.
rows.anchor: فمن نصب فلأجل التضعيف ومن كسر فلالتقاء الساكنين حركت إلى الكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis says he rejects being made God's partner in their obedience to him; the wrongdoers are unbelievers who put obedience in the wrong place.
rows.anchor: إني كفرت بما أشركتمون به من قبل أي لا يمكن أن أكون شريكا لله

rows.speaker: عتبة بن عامر
rows.claim: In a report about intercession, the unbelievers find no intercessor but Iblis; he rises with the foulest smell and repeats that God promised truth while he broke his promise.
rows.anchor: روى عتبة بن عامر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث الشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting سلام in Paradise means God and the angels greet the believers.
rows.anchor: وأدخل الذين آمنوا إلى قوله فيها سلام يسلم الله ويسلم الملائكة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good word is the testimony that there is no god but God, likened to a fruitful date palm; fruit is omitted because eating implies it.
rows.anchor: يعني ما بين الله شبهها كلمة طيبة شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله كشجرة طيبة وهي النخلة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya's visit to Anas included fresh dates, which Anas identified with the tree of the parable; Anas recalled the Prophet reciting the verse over a dish of dates.
rows.anchor: فقال أنس: كل يا أبا العالية فإن هذه من الشجرة التي قال الله في كتابه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Abu Dhubyan transmits Ibn Abbas's view that the tree stands in Paradise; the word of faith is rooted in the believer's heart and rises to God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو ظبيان عن ابن عباس: هذه شجرة في الجنة أصلها ثابت في الأرض

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: A report from al-Dahhak through Ibn Abbas says a column of light shakes when a servant declares God's oneness and Muhammad's servanthood; God forgives the speaker and then stills it.
rows.anchor: وروى مقاتل بن حيان عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تؤتي أكلها means the tree gives its fruit; the interpretations of حين follow in the next excerpt.
rows.anchor: تؤتي أكلها تعطي ثمرها كل حين اختلفوا في الحين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes a known and unknown period; the unknown is the time in which the news will become known, while this verse's known period spans one year to the next.
rows.anchor: إن ابن عباس يقول: الحين حينان حين يعرف ويبدل وحين لا يعرف

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada, and al-Hasan say حين is six months, from the palm's bloom to its fruit-bearing.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وقتادة والحسن: كل ستة أشهر ما بين عرامها إلى حملها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says حين in an oath not to speak means seven months, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: وروى طارق بن عبد الرحمن عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس أنه سئل

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says حين means two months because a palm bears edible fruit only during that period.
rows.anchor: فقال سعيد بن المسيب: الحين شهران لأن النخلة لا يكون فيها أكلها إلا شهرين

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says حين is every morning and evening, when a believer's deeds ascend; Abu Dhubyan also transmits this from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: كل حين كل غدوة وعشية

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says it means every hour through day and night, winter and summer; likewise a believer is never without good.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: كل ساعة ليلا ونهارا، شتاء وصيفا يؤكل في جميع الأوقات

rows.speaker: أبو الحكم
rows.claim: Abu al-Hakam maps the tree's root, trunk, and high branch to faith's affirmation in the heart, confession by the tongue, and bodily action.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو الحكم في تمثيل الله الإيمان بالشجرة فهي أن الشجرة لا تكون شجرة إلا بثلاثة أشياء

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: A report through Ja'far ibn Muhammad and his forefathers says the Prophet defined faith as belief in the heart, declaration by the tongue, and action.
rows.anchor: روى جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه علي بن الحسين عن أبيه الحسين بن علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: حميد الطويل
rows.claim: A report from Anas compares religion to a rooted tree: faith is its root, almsgiving its branch, fasting its veins, calling to God its growth, good character its leaves, and avoiding prohibitions its greenery.
rows.anchor: لحميد الطويل عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The date palm resembles a human: unlike other trees, cutting its top makes it die, and it needs pollination like humans and animals.
rows.anchor: والحكمة في تشبهها إياه بالحنطة من بين سائر الأشجار أنها لما كانت أشبه الأشجار بالإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying calls a fertilized palm grove among the best forms of wealth.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «خير المال سكة مأبورة ومهدة مأمورة»

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar recounts that the Prophet asked which tree never sheds its leaves and resembles a believer; Ibn Umar thought of the date palm but stayed silent from modesty, and his father later regretted that he had not answered.
rows.anchor: حديث ابن عمر: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ذات يوم لأصحابه: «إن شجرة من الشجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report calls the date palm the believers' aunt and says God formed it from a piece of Adam's clay.
rows.anchor: يروى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أكرموا عمتكم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil word means idolatry, and its bad tree is the colocynth.
rows.anchor: ومثل كلمة خبيثة وهي الشرك كشجرة خبيثة هي الحنظلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says this is a parable and that no such tree was created on earth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هذا مثل ضربه الله ولم يخلق هذه الشجرة على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اجتثت means uprooted; Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi say it became loose, al-Dahhak says removed entirely, and al-Mu'arrikh says taken from above the earth.
rows.anchor: اجتثت اقتلعت. قال ابن عباس، والسدي: استرخت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bad tree represents a disbeliever from whom no good comes and whose good speech or deeds do not rise.
rows.anchor: كذلك الكافر لا خير فيه ولا يصعد له قول طيب ولا عمل صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes believers firm through the firm word, the testimony of divine oneness, in worldly life and in the grave after death.
rows.anchor: يثبت الله الذين آمنوا بالقول الثابت يحقق الله إيمانهم وأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says worldly life here means life in the grave before God, and the afterlife means after resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في الحياة في القبر عند الله تعالى وفي الآخرة إذا بعث

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil describes the believer being prepared by Ruman for questioning by Munkar and Nakir, answering correctly, receiving a heavenly opening and comfort; the disbeliever cannot answer and is beaten in a grave opened toward Hell.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: ذلك أن المؤمن إذا مات بعث الله إليه ملكا يقال له: رومان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the disbeliever's failure brings the rebuke لا دريت ولا هديت and a strike whose scream all hear except humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: قال: لا أدري. قال له: لا دريت ولا هديت عشت عصيا ومت شقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil connects the disbeliever's being cursed to the verse about cursers.
rows.anchor: ويعلنه كل من يسمع صوته فذلك قوله ويلعنهم اللاعنون

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib transmits a Prophetic account: angels question the believer in the grave; after his correct answer, God makes him firm and a heavenly caller confirms it.
rows.anchor: روى البراء بن عازب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر قبض روح المؤمن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says angels greet the believer at death and announce Paradise, attend the funeral, then question him in the grave; his grave expands as far as he can see.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: إن المؤمن إذا حضره الموت شهدته الملائكة فسلموا عليه

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Said al-Khudri reports that a grave angel questions the dead about Muhammad; the believer testifies, sees the Hell home he escaped and a Paradise opening, while the hypocrite fails and is beaten with a hammer.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو نضرة عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة

rows.speaker: سهيل بن جابر العتكي
rows.claim: Suhail says he dreamed of the dead Yazid ibn Uthman, who reported that grave angels challenged him about his faith and then asked whether he had written from Jarir ibn Uthman; after he said yes, they condemned Jarir for hating Ali.
rows.anchor: سمعت سهيل بن جابر العتكي يقول: رأيت يزيد بن عثمان بعد موته في المنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God immediately punished people for their wrongs, no creature would remain on earth; instead He delays them to a fixed term, and no one can advance or postpone death by an hour.
rows.anchor: ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بظلمهم فيعاجلهم بالعقوبة على كفرهم وعصيانهم ما ترك عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عليها refers elliptically to the earth's surface, and the fixed term is the end of people's lifespans.
rows.anchor: ما ترك عليها أي على ظهر الأرض كناية عن غير مذكور من دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists assign God what they dislike for themselves, namely daughters, while falsely claiming the best share for themselves.
rows.anchor: ويجعلون لله ما يكرهون لأنفسهم، يعني البنات وتصف ألسنتهم الكذب أن لهم الحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative أن لهم الحسنى explains or restates الكذب; Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan instead read الكذب in the nominative as an adjective for tongues.
rows.anchor: محل (ان) نصب بدل عن الكذب لأنه بيان وترجمة له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan read الكذب with nominative vowels as a description of the lying tongues; الكذب is a plural of كذوب.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: والحسن (الكذب) برفع الكاف والذال والباء على نعت الألسنة

rows.speaker: حيان
rows.claim: Hayyan interprets الحسنى as Paradise in the afterlife, if Muhammad's claim about resurrection is true.
rows.anchor: وقال حيان: يعني بالحسنى الجنة في المعاد إن كان محمد صادقا في البعث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses لا جرم as certainly or indeed.
rows.anchor: لا جرم حقا، وقال ابن عباس: بلى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr say مفرطون means cast far away; Muqatil says abandoned, Qatada says rushed to Hell, and al-Farra says brought forward to it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير: مبعدون. مقاتل: متروكون. قتادة: معجلون إلى النار

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi reads مفرطون with a light rā and kasra, meaning extravagant; Abu Jafar's doubled rā with kasra means neglectful of God's command.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع: (مفرطون) بكسر الراء مع التخفيف أي مسرفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with earlier peoples, Satan beautified their evil deeds and became their helper, companion, supporter, and manager; they face painful punishment.
rows.anchor: فزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم الخبيثة التي كانوا عليها مقيمين فهو وليهم اليوم ناصرهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash say أنعام is masculine or feminine: feminine by collective sense, masculine by its form and lack of a same-form singular.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والأخفش: النعم يذكر ويؤنث فمن أنث فلمعنى الجمع

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i says the pronoun refers to the intended sense of what is in the animals' bellies.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: رد الكناية إلى المراد في بطون ما ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammarians explain the masculine pronoun as deictic reference to this thing or person, supported by several poetic examples.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أراد بطون هذا الشيء، كقول الله: فلما رأى الشمس بازغة قال هذا ربي

rows.speaker: المؤرج
rows.claim: Al-Mu'arrij says the pronoun refers to the relevant part of the herd, since only milk-bearing animals provide milk; the word milk is implicit.
rows.anchor: وقال المؤرج: الكناية مردودة إلى البعض والجزء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farth is the contents of the stomach; milk is pure because it is separated from dung and blood, and it is palatable and does not choke drinkers.
rows.anchor: من بين فرث وهو ما في الكرش فإذا أخرج منه لا يسمى فرثا ودم لبنا خالصا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the animal's food separating in the stomach: blood flows into veins, milk into the udder, and dung remains.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إذا أكلت الدابة العلف واستقر في كرشها لحينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruit from palms and grapes is another sign; منه refers back to those fruits.
rows.anchor: ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب يعني ذلكم أيضا عبرة فيما نسقيكم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One group says sakar is wine, while good provision means vinegar, grapes, dates, and raisins; this is associated with the view that wine is forbidden.
rows.anchor: قال قوم: السكر: الخمر، والرزق الحسن: الخل والعنب والتمر والزبيب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Ibn Amr, and several others are named with the view that sakar means the forbidden product of the fruit and good provision its lawful products.
rows.anchor: وإلى هذا القول ذهب ابن مسعود وابن عمرو وسعيد بن جبير وأيوب وإبراهيم والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says sakar is what is prohibited from the fruits, and good provision is what is lawful.
rows.anchor: وهي رواية عمرو بن سفيان البصري عن ابن عباس قال: السكر: ما حرم من ثمرتها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The continuation says sakar includes foreign peoples' wine, while good provision is what people ferment, make into vinegar, or eat.
rows.anchor: أما السكر فخمور هذه الأعاجم، وأما الرزق الحسن فما تنتبذون وما تخللون وما تأكلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse came before wine was prohibited; its prohibition came later in Surat al-Maida.
rows.anchor: ونزلت هذه الآية ولم يحرم الخمر يومئذ، وإنما نزل تحريمها بعد ذلك في سورة المائدة

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shabi says sakar is what one drinks and good provision what one eats.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: السكر: ما شربت، والرزق الحسن: ما أكلت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's statement that Ethiopians use sakar for vinegar.
rows.anchor: وروى العوفي عن ابن عباس: أن الحبشة يسمون الخل السكر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Another view defines sakar as intoxicating date or raisin infusion once strong, or cooked juice; authorities include al-Dahhak, al-Shabi, al-Nakha'i, and Ibn Abbas in a report.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: السكر: النبيذ المسكر وهو نقيع التمر والزبيب إذا اشتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report distinguishes wine from grapes, sakar from dates, bit from honey, mazr from corn, and bayra from wheat, then forbids every intoxicant.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الخمر ما اتخذ من العنب، والسكر من التمر

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses sakar as taste or flavor, as in saying that something is a flavor for you.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: السكر: الطعم، يقال: هذا سكر لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses sakar to mean flavor.
rows.anchor: وأنشد: جعلت عيب الأكرمين سكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's inspiration to bees means placing the knowledge in their hearing or instincts; النحل are honey-producing wasps, with نحلة as the singular.
rows.anchor: وأوحى ربك إلى النحل أي ألقى [على مسامعها] أو قذف في أنفسها ففهمته

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says what people build trellises for means grapevines.
rows.anchor: ومن الشجر ومما يعرشون يبنون، وقال ابن زيد: هو الكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From every fruit is not universal, as in other verses that say a person received everything or a wind destroyed everything.
rows.anchor: ثم كلي من كل الثمرات ليس معنى الكل العموم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Some say ذللا describes the bee's routes as made easy; Mujahid says no place it travels is rugged.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: الذلل يعني الطرق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Others, including Qatada, take ذللا as describing the bees themselves: obedient and compliant.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة وغيره: يعني مطيعة منقادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bees' drink emerges in differing colors and contains healing for people.
rows.anchor: يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه أبيض وأحمر وأصفر فيه شفاء للناس

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report from Abu Said says the Prophet repeatedly told a man with an ill brother to give him honey; after another dose, the brother recovered.
rows.anchor: يروى أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إن أخي يشتكي بطنه

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says شيء is a substitute for provision, meaning the false gods own none of it, little or much.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: هو بدل من الرزق وهو في معنى: ما لا يملكون من الرزق شيئا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says شيء is accusative because provision governs it, as earth gathers the living and the dead and as one feeds an orphan.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: نصب (شيئا) بوقوع الرزق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot do anything; people must not compare God to created things or give Him a partner, because He has no equal and knows their error.
rows.anchor: فلا تضربوا لله الأمثال يعني الأشباه والأشكال فيشبهوه بخلقه ويجعلون له شريكا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud defines squandering as spending money outside its proper right.
rows.anchor: فقال: إنفاق المال في غير حقه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says spending all one's money on what is right is not waste, but spending even a small amount on falsehood is waste.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لو أنفق إنسان ماله كله في [الحق ما كان] تبذيرا

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq points to a house built with plaster and brick as an example of waste under Ibn Masud's definition.
rows.anchor: فأتى على دار تبنى بجص وآجر فقال: هذا التبذير في قول عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The squanderers are allies and followers of devils; Arabic calls someone who follows a group's custom its brother, and Satan was ungrateful to his Lord.
rows.anchor: إن المبذرين كانوا إخوان الشياطين أولياؤهم وأعوانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command about turning away was revealed concerning Munajji, Bilal, Suhayb, Salim, and Khabbab, who asked the Prophet for needs he could not meet; he turned away out of embarrassment.
rows.anchor: نزلت في منجع وبلال وصهيب وسالم وخباب، كانوا يسألون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When unable to meet those asking for their due, the Prophet should speak gently and promise well while hoping for provision from God.
rows.anchor: ابتغاء رحمة من ربك ابتغاء رزق من الله ترجوها أن يأتيك فقل لهم قولا ميسورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hand tied to the neck means withholding money due in rightful spending; do not be miserly.
rows.anchor: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك يعني ولا تمسك يدك عن النفقة في الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not give away everything, leaving yourself blamed by those asking and depleted with nothing left to spend.
rows.anchor: ولا تبسطها بالعطاء كل البسط فتعطي جميع ما تملك فتقعد ملوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: محسورا means left exhausted and empty; the root also describes a spent animal and a weary eye, and Qatada adds regret over past spending.
rows.anchor: محسورا منقطعا بك لا شيء عندك تنفقه، فقال: حسرته بالمسألة

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir recounts that a boy asked for a shirt for his mother; the Prophet gave away his only shirt, remained naked, and missed prayer, prompting the verse about avoiding total depletion.
rows.anchor: قال جابر بن عبد الله: بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاعد فيما بين الصحابة أتاه صبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading كان سيئة means the conduct mentioned is bad and disliked by God.
rows.anchor: (كان سيئة) أي سيء بما ذكرنا ووعدنا عليك عند ربك مكروها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers this reading because the passage contains commands and prohibitions and Ubayy's reading كان سيئاته supports treating كل ذلك as the prohibited matters.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد هذه القراءة لما ذكرنا من المعنى

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b reads كان سيئاته, making the whole listed material from the prohibition against killing children a bad deed.
rows.anchor: وهي ما روى أبو عبيد عن حجاج عن هارون في قراءة [أبي بن كعب]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مكروها is not a second predicate without rearrangement; one analysis puts disliked before bad, while another coordinates it as a separate predicate.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل: هلا جعلت مكروها خبر ثان، قلنا: في الكلام تقديم وتأخير

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans say the wording returns to meaning because سيئة means a sin, while the stated wisdom and prohibitions are the referent.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل الكوفة: رجع إلى المعنى، لأن السيئة الذنب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the eighteen verses were written on Moses' tablets and correspond to the Ten Commandments in the Torah.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: [الثمان عشرة] آية كانت في ألواح موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address rebukes Arab polytheists for claiming God chose sons for them but took angels as daughters, which is a grave assertion.
rows.anchor: أفأصفاكم اختاركم واختصكم ربكم بالبنين واتخذ من الملائكة إناثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use the doubled form صرفنا; al-Hasan reads it with a light form.
rows.anchor: قرأه العامة: بالتشديد على التكثير. وقرأ الحسن: صرفنا بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم الحسين
rows.claim: One explanation says God diversified the Qur'an among promises, warnings, commands, prohibitions, clear and ambiguous verses, abrogation, stories, and examples; another says it came down in portions through repeated angelic visits.
rows.anchor: سمعت أبا القاسم الحسين يقول: بحضره الإمام أبي الطيب لقوله تعالى صرفنا معنيان

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yahya, al-A'mash, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read ليذكروا with a light consonant form; the remaining readers use the doubled form, preferred by Abu Ubayd as meaning remember.
rows.anchor: قرأ يحيى والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي ليذكروا مخففا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder and repeated forms increase the unbelievers' flight and distance from the truth.
rows.anchor: وما يزيدهم أي التصريف والتذكير إلا نفورا ذهابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If there were other gods with God as the polytheists claim, they would seek a path of nearness to the Lord of the Throne.
rows.anchor: قل يا محمد لهؤلاء المشركين لو كان معه آلهة كما يقولون

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Hafs read يقولون with yā; the other readers use tā.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحفص: يقولون بالياء. الباقون: بالتاء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the imagined gods would recognize God's favor and superiority over them and pursue what brings them close to Him.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: يقول لو كان [الأمر] كما يقولون إذا لعرفوا الله فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say the hypothetical gods would seek to contend and fight with God as earthly kings do with one another.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: إذا لطلبوا مع الله منازعة وقتالا، كفعل ملوك الدنيا بعضهم ببعض

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A'mash, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read the following address with tā; Abu Ubayd prefers this reading, with علوا as the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: الأعمش وحمزة والكسائي، واختاره أبو عبيد عنهم بالتاء علوا كبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cave story, one man returns all the wages he had invested for an absent worker; he asks God to release them if he acted for God's sake, and the rock splits until they see light.
rows.anchor: فعرضتها عليه جميعا فقال: يا عبد الله، لا تسخر بي إن لم تتصدق علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second man resisted a poor woman who yielded to sex only to feed her children; when she invoked God, he stopped and compensated her, and the rock opened farther.
rows.anchor: فأبت علي، وذهبت ورجعت ثلاث مرات وقلت: لا والله ما هو دون نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third man waited with milk in his hand until his sleeping elderly parents woke, then served them first and asked God to open the rock.
rows.anchor: فوجدتهما ناما، فشق علي أن أوقضهما، وشق علي أن أترك غنمي

rows.speaker: النعمان
rows.claim: Al-Numan says the Prophet described the mountain saying طاق as God opened it and let the men out.
rows.anchor: قال النعمان لكأني أسمع من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies al-Raqim as a valley between Ghatafan and Aylah, the valley containing the cave companions.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الرقيم واد بين غطفان وأيلة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b says al-Raqim was the companions' town; on this reading the word comes from a valley's water-place, contrasted with its banks.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب هي قريتهم. وهو على هذا التأويل من رقمة الوادي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says al-Raqim was an iron or lead tablet inscribed with the companions' names and story and placed at the cave entrance; the root means writing or marking.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: الرقيم لوح من حديد، وقيل: من رصاص

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq narrates that pagan Roman ruler Decius persecuted Christians in Ephesus; eight noble youths kept monotheism, prayed and fasted, then fled the forced choice between idol worship and death after believers were tortured and displayed on the city walls.
rows.anchor: فقال محمد بن إسحاق بن يسار: مرج أهل الإنجيل وعظمت فيهم الخطايا وطغت فيهم الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths' prayer declares God alone as Lord of heaven and earth and says invoking another deity would be an outrageous falsehood; they ask for the persecution to be lifted.
rows.anchor: ربنا رب السماوات والأرض لن ندعوا من دونه إلها لقد قلنا إذا شططا
